title: Human Body Schema
description: Comprehensive anatomical data schema for human body modeling. Covers skeletal, muscular, connective, nervous, vascular, organ, appearance, kinematics, dynamics, derivation, constitutive, and geometry subsystems. Generated from Zod v3 TypeScript source via dedup post-processor. Schema version 3.0.0.

schemaVersion.description: Must match the schema version this instance was created against

rotation.description: Rotation as Euler angles (degrees, XYZ intrinsic order)

depth.description: Maximum depth in cm (for non-cylindrical bones)

centerOfMass.description: Center of mass position in the bone's local frame (cm). Typically expressed as a fraction of segment length from proximal end. [Authority: subordinate to BodySegment.centerOfMass for dynamics — segment-level values are authoritative for multibody analysis; bone-level values are anatomical detail for single-bone models.]

inertiaTensor.description: Moment of inertia tensor about the center of mass in the bone's local frame (g·cm²). [Authority: subordinate to BodySegment.inertiaTensor for dynamics — a segment may aggregate multiple bones into a single rigid body.]

parentBoneId.description: Parent bone in the skeletal hierarchy; null for root (e.g. pelvis)

connectedBoneIds.description: IDs of bones articulated by this joint (2–4, ordered: proximal first)

axes.description: Joint coordinate system axes per Grood-Suntay convention

limits.description: Range of motion limits by anatomical plane

localPosition.description: Local position on the bone surface (cm)

surfaceArea.description: Surface area of attachment in cm²

description.description: Anatomical description, e.g. 'lateral epicondyle of humerus'

origin.description: Where the muscle originates — typically the proximal, more stable attachment

insertion.description: Where the muscle inserts — typically the distal, more mobile attachment

pennationAngle.description: Angle of fibers relative to the force-generating axis (degrees). 0 = parallel.

optimalFiberLength.description: Optimal sarcomere length for max force in cm

pcsa.description: Physiological cross-sectional area in cm² (computed: volume / optimalFiberLength)

maxContractionVelocity.description: V_max in optimal fiber lengths per second (L₀/s)

primaryArteryId.description: Primary arterial supply if vascular system is modeled

antagonistIds.description: Muscles opposing this muscle's primary action

synergistIds.description: Muscles assisting this muscle's primary action

isVital.description: Whether destruction of this organ is immediately life-threatening

pairedOrgan.description: Whether this organ exists bilaterally (e.g. kidneys, lungs)

laterality.description: Anatomical side; required when pairedOrgan is true

path.description: Centerline path as ordered control points (cm)

parentVesselId.description: Upstream vessel this branches from; null for aorta/vena cava

hasValves.description: Whether the vein has anti-reflux valves

density.description: Capillary density in vessels per mm²

name.description: Anatomical name (e.g. 'anterior cruciate ligament', 'medial collateral ligament')

originPosition.description: Attachment point on the origin bone in its local frame (cm)

insertionPosition.description: Attachment point on the insertion bone in its local frame (cm)

jointId.description: Joint this ligament spans and stabilizes

linearStiffness.description: Linear region stiffness in N/mm (slope of the force-displacement curve past the toe region)

toeRegionStrain.description: Strain at which the toe region ends and linear region begins (dimensionless, typically 0.03–0.06)

ultimateStrain.description: Strain at failure (dimensionless, typically 0.10–0.15 for healthy ligament)

referenceStrain.description: Strain at the reference pose (anatomical position). Negative = slack, positive = pre-tensioned.

ligaments.description: Joint ligaments — passive restraints connecting bone to bone

name.description: Anatomical name (e.g. 'femoral condyle articular cartilage', 'medial meniscus')

thickness.description: Average thickness in mm (articular cartilage: typically 1–7 mm)

youngsModulus.description: Equilibrium aggregate modulus in MPa (articular cartilage: 0.5–1.5 MPa)

cartilage.description: Articular cartilage and fibrocartilage (menisci, labra, discs)

spinalRoots.description: Contributing spinal nerve roots (e.g. ['C5', 'C6'] for musculocutaneous nerve)

parentNerveId.description: Parent nerve this branches from; null for roots/trunks (e.g. sciatic)

path.description: Centerline path of the nerve as ordered control points (cm, global frame at anatomical position)

conductionVelocity.description: Motor conduction velocity in m/s (normal: 40–80 m/s for motor, varies by fiber type)

dermatome.description: Skin region innervated for sensation (e.g. 'lateral forearm' for musculocutaneous)

nerves.description: Peripheral nerves — motor, sensory, mixed, autonomic

radiusTop.description: Top radius in cm (0 = cone apex)

height.description: Height along local Y axis in cm

radii.description: Semi-axis radii (x, y, z) in cm

halfExtents.description: Half-widths along each axis in cm

radius.description: Cylinder and hemisphere radius in cm

height.description: Total height including caps in cm

majorRadius.description: Distance from center to tube center in cm

children.description: Operands. For 'subtract': children[0] is the base, children[1..n] are subtracted.
Operands. For 'subtract': children[0] is the base, children[1..n] are subtracted.

csgTree.description: Root of the CSG tree defining the bone shape

collisionHull.description: Preferred broad-phase collision shape (computed from CSG tree if absent)

lods.description: Level-of-detail meshes. lods[0] is the highest resolution.

name.description: Standard anatomical name (e.g., 'lateral_epicondyle', 'greater_trochanter', 'medial_malleolus'). Use snake_case ISB terminology.

nearestVertexByLOD.description: Map from LOD level (as string key '0', '1', ...) to nearest vertex index in that LOD. Allows snapping the landmark to the mesh surface at any resolution.

landmarks.description: Named anatomical landmarks on the bone surface

isClosed.description: Whether the mesh is a closed (watertight) manifold — required for volume calculation

isManifold.description: Whether the mesh is 2-manifold (every edge shared by exactly 2 triangles)

method.description: How the mesh geometry was obtained

resolution.description: Source voxel/scan resolution in mm (for imaging-derived meshes)

citation.description: Bibliographic reference for the source data

uri.description: URI to the mesh file (HTTPS, file://, or asset:// scheme)

byteSize.description: Expected file size in bytes (for progress indication and cache validation)

contentHash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file content (for integrity verification)

level.description: LOD level (1 = first reduction from base)

lodVariants.description: Lower-resolution variants for distance-based LOD switching

upAxis.description: Which axis is 'up' in the file (Y = glTF/OpenGL, Z = Blender/3ds Max)

units.description: Length unit of the vertex coordinates

coordinateSpace.description: Coordinate space metadata — consumer must transform to match schema convention (Y-up, cm, right-handed)

landmarks.description: Anatomical landmarks (positions in bone-local frame, independent of mesh resolution)

boneGeometries.description: Geometric shape data for bones. Each entry references a bone via boneId. Supports three representations: parametric_csg (compact procedural), indexed_mesh (inline triangles), or external_asset (URI reference).

parentFrameId.description: Parent frame ID; null = this IS the global frame

position.description: Translation from the parent frame origin (cm)

poseInParent.description: Pose (position + orientation) of this frame's origin in the parent frame

referenceFrames.description: Defined coordinate frames (global, segment, joint). At least the global frame should be present for kinematic analysis.

boneIds.description: Bones that compose this rigid segment (ordered: proximal first)

proximalJointId.description: Joint at the proximal end; null for root segment (pelvis)

distalJointIds.description: Joints at the distal end(s). Usually 1, but pelvis has 2 (L/R hip) + spine.

centerOfMass.description: Center of mass in the segment's local frame (cm). Convention: expressed as offset from proximal joint center. [Authority: authoritative for multibody dynamics — overrides per-bone centerOfMass when a segment aggregates multiple bones.]

centerOfMassRatio.description: CoM position as fraction of segment length from proximal end (0 = proximal, 1 = distal). De Leva (1996) tables provide standard values per segment.

inertiaTensor.description: Moment of inertia tensor about the CoM in the segment's local frame (kg·cm²). [Authority: authoritative for multibody dynamics — overrides per-bone inertiaTensor when a segment aggregates multiple bones.]

segmentLength.description: Length from proximal to distal joint center (cm)

sagittal.description: ρ about the mediolateral axis (sagittal plane motion)

frontal.description: ρ about the anteroposterior axis (frontal plane motion)

transverse.description: ρ about the longitudinal axis (transverse plane rotation)

gyrationRatios.description: Normalized radii of gyration (k/L). See De Leva 1996, Table 4.

segments.description: Rigid body segments (thigh, shank, foot, etc.). Required for kinematics/dynamics analysis.

timestamp.description: Time in seconds from the start of a recording or sequence

rootSegmentId.description: Which segment is the kinematic root (usually pelvis)

rootPose.description: Position and orientation of the root segment in the global frame. This anchors the entire kinematic chain in world space.

jointStates.description: Joint angle state for every articulated joint (ordered: proximal to distal)

globalPose.description: Position + orientation of the segment's local frame in the global frame

segmentStates.description: [Computed] World-space state of each segment, derived from rootPose + jointStates via FK

currentPose.description: Current body configuration. If absent, the body is in the default (anatomical) position defined by bone transforms.

savedPoses.description: Library of named poses (e.g. anatomical position, T-pose, seated, mid-stance)

interpolation.description: Recommended interpolation between keyframes. 'slerp' for rotations, 'linear'/'cubic_spline' for positions.

targetSegmentId.description: Segment this gravitational force acts on (applied at its CoM)

gravitationalAcceleration.description: Gravitational acceleration in cm/s² (default: 981 cm/s² = 9.81 m/s²)

applicationPoint.description: Point where force is effectively applied in global frame (cm). For pennate muscles, this is the effective insertion point along the tendon.

activationLevel.description: Neural activation level (0 = fully relaxed, 1 = max voluntary contraction)

currentLength.description: Current muscle-tendon unit length in cm

contractionVelocity.description: Rate of change of muscle length in cm/s (negative = shortening)

momentArm.description: Perpendicular distance from the joint center to the muscle's line of action (cm). τ = F × momentArm gives the moment contribution.

centerOfPressure.description: Point of application on the ground plane in global frame (cm). COP = point where the resultant GRF acts with zero horizontal moment.

anteroposterior.description: A-P component in N (+X = anterior = braking is negative)

mediolateral.description: M-L component in N (+Z = right lateral)

freeMoment.description: Vertical free moment (torque about Y axis) in N·cm

jointId.description: Joint where this reaction force acts

applicationPoint.description: Joint center position in global frame (cm)

compression.description: Along the bone's longitudinal axis (N). Positive = compressive.

componentsInJCS.description: Force decomposed into the joint coordinate system

applicationPoint.description: Point of application in global frame (cm)

targetSegmentId.description: Segment this force is applied to

description.description: What this force represents (e.g. 'barbell load', 'wind gust')

distributed.description: Whether this is a distributed load (pressure) or a point force

applicationPoint.description: Effective point of application in global frame (cm)

strain.description: Current strain (ΔL/L₀, dimensionless). Ligaments typically fail at 0.06–0.15.

stiffness.description: Linear stiffness in N/cm (slope of force-displacement curve)

segmentAcceleration.description: Linear acceleration of the segment CoM (cm/s²)

applicationPoint.description: Point of contact in global frame (cm)

normalForce.description: Normal component at the contact surface (N)

relativeVelocity.description: Velocity of segment relative to fluid (cm/s)

displacedVolume.description: Volume of fluid displaced by the segment (cm³)

fluidDensity.description: Density of the fluid in g/cm³ (water ≈ 1.0)

centerOfBuoyancy.description: Centroid of displaced volume in global frame (cm)

forces.description: All forces acting on the body at this instant

magnitude.description: Moment magnitude in N·cm (positive = right-hand rule about axis)

componentsInJCS.description: Moment decomposed into JCS axes (standard clinical reporting)

moments.description: All moments (may be computed from forces)

segmentId.description: Body segment involved in the contact

isActive.description: Whether this contact is currently engaged

netForce.description: [Computed] Resultant of all forces (N). Zero = static equilibrium.

netMoment.description: [Computed] Resultant moment about the whole-body CoM (N·cm).

equilibrium.description: [Computed] Equilibrium check — residuals should be near zero for valid solutions

loadingConditions.description: Force/moment snapshots. Each references a pose and contains all forces at that instant.

forces.description: All forces acting on this segment

moments.description: All moments acting on this segment

freeBodyDiagrams.description: [Computed] Per-segment FBDs derived from loading conditions

inputFields.description: Schema fields that serve as inputs to this derivation

outputField.description: Schema field that this derivation computes. Must be a field annotated [Computed].

invertible.description: Whether the equation can be solved in reverse (output → inputs)

absolute.description: Absolute tolerance in the output field's units

consistencyTolerance.description: Tolerance for consistency verification. If |stored - derived| > tolerance, the field is inconsistent.

dependsOn.description: IDs of DerivationRules whose outputs are inputs to this rule (establishes DAG order)

derivationGraph.description: Declarative derivation DAG. Each rule declares: output = f(inputs) with a named physical law, tolerance, and dependency ordering. Enables mechanical consistency checking of [Computed] fields.

widthParameter.description: Width of the Gaussian active force-length curve (γ). f_L(L̃) = exp(-((L̃ - 1)/γ)²). Typical: 0.45–0.56. Ref: Thelen, J Biomech 36(6):853–862, 2003.

minActiveForceLengthRatio.description: Minimum normalized length for active force production (L̃_min). Typically ~0.5.

maxActiveForceLengthRatio.description: Maximum normalized length for active force production (L̃_max). Typically ~1.5.

concentricCurveShape.description: Shape factor for concentric (shortening) force-velocity curve (A_f). Smaller = more curved. Typical: 0.1–0.4. Ref: Thelen (2003).

eccentricForceMax.description: Maximum eccentric force as multiple of F_max (F_len). Muscles can produce ~1.4–1.8× F_max eccentrically. Ref: Katz (1939), Thelen (2003).

eccentricCurveShape.description: Shape factor for eccentric (lengthening) curve. Typical: 0.1–0.3.

strainAtMaxForce.description: Normalized strain at which passive force = F_max (ε_M). f_PE(L̃) = (exp(k_PE × (L̃ - 1)/ε_M) - 1) / (exp(k_PE) - 1). Typical: 0.5–0.7. Ref: Thelen (2003).

exponentialShape.description: Shape of the passive force exponential (k_PE). Typical: 3–5.

normalizedSlackLength.description: Tendon slack length / optimal fiber length (L_T_slack / L_opt). Typical: 0.5–10.

strainAtMaxIsometricForce.description: Tendon strain at F_max. Typical: 0.033 (3.3%). Ref: Zajac (1989).

tendonCompliance.description: Tendon elasticity parameters. If absent, tendon is assumed rigid.

equation.description: The Hill model constraint in symbolic form

violationSeverity.description: Severity when a muscle force exceeds the achievable envelope

toleranceFraction.description: Fractional tolerance above the computed envelope before flagging a violation. 0.1 = allow 10% overshoot (accounts for parameter uncertainty).

maxStrain.description: Strain at transition from toe to linear region (ε_toe). Typical: 0.03–0.06.

curveExponent.description: Exponent for the quadratic toe region: F = k_toe × ε^n. Typical: 2.

stiffness.description: Stiffness in the linear region in N/mm (slope of force-displacement). Varies widely by ligament.

interceptStrain.description: Strain-axis intercept of the linear extrapolation (ε₀). F = k × (ε - ε₀) for ε > ε_toe.

ultimateStrain.description: Strain at rupture (ε_fail). Typical: 0.10–0.15 for healthy ligament.

ultimateLoad.description: Force at rupture in N. Highly variable: ACL ~2,160 N young adult.

equation.const: F_lig = piecewise(ε ≤ 0: 0, ε ≤ ε_toe: k_toe×ε^n, ε ≤ ε_fail: k×(ε-ε₀), ε > ε_fail: FAILURE)

strainTolerance.description: Absolute strain tolerance for consistency checking

contactForce.description: Path to contact/joint reaction force on the cartilage surface

aggregateModulus.description: Equilibrium aggregate modulus H_A in MPa. Healthy articular: 0.5–1.5 MPa.

maxContactPressure.description: Maximum tolerable contact pressure in MPa before damage. Articular cartilage: ~5–10 MPa static, ~15–25 MPa dynamic. Ref: Torzilli et al., J Biomech 32(10):1063–1073, 1999.

equation.const: σ = F / A ≤ σ_max AND ε = σ / H_A ≤ thickness
equation.description: Contact stress must not exceed damage threshold; deformation must not exceed thickness

pressureTolerance.description: Tolerance in MPa for pressure violation threshold

jointReactionForce.description: Path to JointReactionForce acting on this bone

corticalTensileYield.description: Cortical bone tensile yield stress in MPa. Ref: Reilly & Burstein (1974).

corticalCompressiveYield.description: Cortical bone compressive yield stress in MPa.

trabecularCompressiveYield.description: Trabecular bone compressive yield stress in MPa (highly variable: 2–12 MPa).

fatigueReductionFactor.description: Reduction factor for cyclic loading fatigue. Effective yield ≈ yield × factor for repetitive loading.

equation.const: σ_bone = F / A ≤ σ_yield (rigid body assumption valid when σ_bone << σ_yield)
equation.description: Bone stress must remain well below yield for rigid body dynamics to be valid

jointAngle.description: Path to JointState.angles for the relevant DOF

jointLimit.description: Path to JointSchema.limits for this DOF

bufferAngle.description: Angle (degrees) before the hard limit where passive resistance begins. Typical: 3–10°.

exponentialStiffness.description: Stiffness of the exponential barrier in N·cm/degree.

equation.const: θ_min + buffer ≤ θ ≤ θ_max - buffer (passive resistance outside this range)
equation.description: Joint angle should be within ROM limits; passive torque increases exponentially at boundaries

constitutiveLaws.description: Constitutive law collection. Each law declares an inequality/envelope constraint on field values (e.g. muscle force ≤ Hill model envelope). Includes model validity boundaries declaring when assumptions break down.

FieldRef.description: Dot-separated path to a schema field. Use [*] for array iteration, [i] for indexed access. Examples: 'muscles[*].pcsa', 'loadingConditions[*].equilibrium.netForce'

nerveId.description: Reference to a Nerve entity if the nervous system is modeled

spinalRoots.description: Spinal nerve roots (e.g. ['C5', 'C6']). Format: C=cervical, T=thoracic, L=lumbar, S=sacral + level number

indices.description: Triangle indices into the vertex arrays. Length must be 3 × triangleCount. Winding order: counter-clockwise (right-hand rule for outward normals).

positions.description: Flat array of vertex positions [x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ...] in cm, bone-local frame. Length must be 3 × vertexCount.

normals.description: Flat array of vertex normals [nx0,ny0,nz0, ...]. Length must equal positions.length. Unit-length vectors.

uvs.description: Flat array of UV coordinates [u0,v0, u1,v1, ...] for texture mapping. Length must be 2 × vertexCount.

colors.description: Flat array of per-vertex colors [r0,g0,b0,a0, ...] as uint8. Length must be 4 × vertexCount. Useful for encoding bone density maps.

name.description: Name of the physical law or definition

equation.description: Symbolic equation in standard math notation. Variables correspond to inputFields and outputField. Examples: 'PCSA = V / L_opt', 'F_net = Σ Fᵢ', 'r_com = Σ(mᵢrᵢ) / Σ(mᵢ)'

reference.description: Literature reference. Example: 'Zajac, CRC Crit Rev Biomed Eng 17(4):359–411, 1989'

domain.description: Which branch of mechanics this law belongs to

biologicalSex.description: Biological sex — affects default proportional ratios

legLength.description: Greater trochanter to floor in cm

muscleMassPercentage.description: Percentage of body mass that is skeletal muscle (typical: 30–45%)

fatPercentage.description: Body fat percentage (essential fat: ~3% male, ~12% female)

vertexIndices.description: Vertex indices (in LOD 0) belonging to this region. Max 500k (matches vertex count ceiling).

relatedEntityId.description: ID of the related entity (e.g., TendonId for attachment, CartilageId for articular)

assumption.description: The modeling assumption this boundary protects. Examples: 'rigid body', 'small deformations', 'quasi-static loading'

validWhen.description: Condition under which the assumption holds, as a human-readable predicate. Example: 'bone stress < yield stress (~130 MPa cortical, ~5 MPa trabecular)'

violatedWhen.description: Condition under which the assumption breaks down. Example: 'impact loading with strain rate > 1/s'

consequence.description: What goes wrong when the assumption is violated. Example: 'bone deformation is non-negligible; rigid body dynamics underestimates joint forces'

reference.description: Literature reference for the validity domain
